answer: The reflow ovens (RF-01, RF-02, and RF-03) used a total of 1,246.1 kWh last weekend, costing NT$10,903.0 [data: get_energy].

The demand on 16 June exceeded the contract capacity on two intervals. The peak demand was 1324.4 kW at 08:15, which is 1.06 times the contract capacity of 1250.0 kW. Another interval with demand above the contract was at 08:00 with 1307.1 kW [data: get_demand].

According to the plant documents, reflow ovens must be switched off rather than left in standby over the weekend to prevent idle energy consumption. A reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating, which is 25.2 kW, for as long as it is left. This results in significant energy waste, as a properly switched-off oven uses about 340-350 kWh per oven-weekend. In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend and the weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh against about 346 kWh normal. The excess is about 1,210 kWh from a single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Loads that must never be shed are critical equipment such as safety systems, essential machinery, and life-support systems [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Trigger conditions].
